`import type` tells the reader, and every tool that compiles one file at a time, that the import is gone at runtime. A plain `import` of something that's only used as a type leaves that open. The module may or may not be loaded for its side effects, depending on the compiler and its settings.

`--fix` adds the `type` keyword, and splits the import if it also brings in values.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports" = ["error", {
  prefer = "type-imports", # "type-imports" or "no-type-imports"
  # "separate-type-imports" or "inline-type-imports"
  fixStyle = "separate-type-imports",
  disallowTypeAnnotations = true,
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { User } from "./models";

export function greet(user: User) {
  return `Hello, ${user.name}`;
}
```

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { User, createUser } from "./models";

export const admin: User = createUser("Ada");
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import type { User } from "./models";
import { createUser } from "./models";

export const admin: User = createUser("Ada");
```

{/* good */}
```ts
import { type User, createUser } from "./models";

export const admin: User = createUser("Ada");
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prefer` | `"type-imports"` | `"type-imports"` requires `import type`. `"no-type-imports"` reports it. |
| `fixStyle` | `"separate-type-imports"` | What `--fix` writes: `import type { User }`, or with `"inline-type-imports"`, `import { type User }`. Both forms are accepted in your code with either value. |
| `disallowTypeAnnotations` | `true` | Also report `import("./models")` in a type. |

{/* bad {"options": [{"prefer": "no-type-imports"}]} */}
```ts
import type { User } from "./models";

export type Users = User[];
```

{/* good {"options": [{"prefer": "no-type-imports"}]} */}
```ts
import { User } from "./models";

export type Users = User[];
```

By default, a type written as `import()` is reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
export type Users = import("./models").User[];
```

{/* good {"options": [{"disallowTypeAnnotations": false}]} */}
```ts
export type Users = import("./models").User[];
```

## When not to use it

TypeScript's `verbatimModuleSyntax` option makes a missing `import type` a compile error. If it's on, you only need this rule for its fix.

With `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata` both on, TypeScript needs some imported types at runtime, and `import type` removes them. The rule leaves the imports alone in a file that has a decorator. With `--type-aware` it reads both settings from your `tsconfig.json`, and checks such a file too if one of them is off.

{/* good */}
```ts
import { Database } from "./database";

@Injectable()
export class Users {
  constructor(private database: Database) {}
}
```
